1.name: Technical University
1.description: Leading engineering and technology programs with state-of-the-art research facilities.
1.longDescription:
Technical University of Varna is the second-largest state technical university in Bulgaria, founded in 1962. It holds institutional accreditation with the highest rating of Very Good for a six-year period, awarded by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency (NEAA). It is the first university in Bulgaria to receive institutional accreditation from the European University Association. The university is certified under ISO 9001:2008 and has an extensive international network with 155 partner universities from 47 countries through Erasmus+ and other programmes.

The university comprises 4 faculties — Mechanical Engineering (MTF), Shipbuilding (KF), Electrical Engineering (EF), and Computer Systems & Automation (FITA) — along with the Dobrudzha Technological College in Dobrich, an in-house College of TU-Varna, a Research Institute, and a High Technology Park. The campus spans 200 decares and features over 230 modernly equipped laboratories, 50+ lecture halls, a sports complex, 6 student dormitories, a canteen, library, career centre, CISCO Academy, Maritime Qualification Centre, Autodesk Authorized Training Centre, and a Doctoral Centre.

Over 60,000 students have graduated since its founding across 33 bachelor's and 92 master's programmes and doctoral programmes. The university is a partner of leading companies including Siemens, ABB, Festo, Schneider Electric, National Instruments, Autodesk, Schwarz IT, and MTG Delfin shipyard.

Several programmes are offered tuition-free: Electric Power Engineering, Power Supply & Electrical Equipment, Naval Architecture & Marine Technology, and Heat Power Engineering & Investment Design. Rector: Prof. Dr. Dragomir Plamenov.

2.name: Medical University
2.description: Bulgaria's leading medical university with top-ranked clinical training and research programs.
2.longDescription:
Medical University of Varna (Prof. Dr. Paraskev Stoyanov) is a leading Bulgarian medical university founded in 1961. It is accredited with the highest rating by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency (NEAA) and holds the EFQM Excellence Model recognition. The university comprises 4 faculties — Medicine, Dental Medicine, Pharmacy, and Public Health — along with the Medical College - Varna and affiliates in Shumen, Veliko Tarnovo, and Burgas.

The university has over 7,000 students, 2,000 of whom are international students from 56 countries. The campus features modern simulation centers, clinical bases at the University Hospital St. Marina, research laboratories, a library, sports facilities, and student dormitories.

International students can study Medicine, Dental Medicine, and Pharmacy in English. Nursing and Midwifery are tuition-free. The university has 100+ international partner institutions and active Erasmus+ exchange programs.

Over 50,000 alumni have graduated since its founding. Rector: Prof. Dr. Valentin Ignatov.

3.name: University of Economics – Varna
3.description: Bulgaria's oldest specialised economics university, offering business, finance, IT, management and tourism programs by the Black Sea.
3.longDescription:
The University of Economics – Varna (UE-Varna) is one of Bulgaria's oldest and most prestigious higher schools of economics, founded on 14 May 1920 as the Higher School of Commerce. It is the second economics-focused university established in Bulgaria and a landmark of the city of Varna — its central building is a cultural-heritage site next to the Sea Garden and was awarded the Building of the Year prize in 2015. The university is accredited by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency (NEAA) and is the only Bulgarian higher-education institution certified with the European Solidarity Corps Programme Quality Label. It is featured in the Times Higher Education World University Impact Rankings.

The university is organised into 4 faculties — Finance and Accounting, Economics, Information Technologies (Informatics) and Management — together with the College of Tourism – Varna and a Department of Language Learning. It offers 28 bachelor's programmes (23 in Bulgarian, 3 in English and 1 in Russian), 29 master's programmes (25 in Bulgarian, 4 in English), 16 doctoral programmes and 20+ post-graduate qualification programmes.

Today UE-Varna has over 7,500 Bulgarian and international students taught by more than 230 full-time lecturers, including 100+ professors and associate professors. The campus offers 110+ lecture and study halls, a 600-seat Aula auditorium and a library of over 350,000 volumes. More than 155,000 economists and professionals have graduated from the university over its century of history.

The university maintains an extensive international network of almost 190 partner universities and cooperation with 258 institutions from 45 countries through Erasmus+, CEEPUS, DukeNET, BusiNET, the Magellan Exchange and EEA/Norway grants, and works with over 1,800 corporate and public-administration partners. Rector: Prof. Dr. Evgeni Stanimirov.

4.name: Naval University
4.description: Bulgaria's oldest maritime school — training naval officers and merchant-marine professionals since 1881.
4.longDescription:
The Nikola Vaptsarov Naval Academy is Bulgaria's oldest maritime and technical school, founded in 1881 as a Maritime School and named in 1949 after the poet Nikola Vaptsarov, a 1926 graduate. It is the country's most authoritative centre for maritime education, training both military naval officers and civilian merchant-marine professionals.

The academy is organised into two faculties — the Faculty of Navigation and the Faculty of Engineering — each with six departments, supported by a Department of Postgraduate Training and Distance Learning, a Professional Junior-Officers' College, a Cyber Operations Training Centre and a research section. It offers 12 bachelor's, 13 master's and 9 doctoral programmes, with around 3,000 students and cadets.

Training complies with the IMO STCW 78/95 convention; the academy has been on the IMO "White List" since 2000, is ISO 9001 certified and received full university accreditation in 2001. It is consistently ranked among the world's leading maritime universities (placed 2nd–4th among 70 institutions in international assessments). Facilities include unique navigation, engine-room and LNG-bunkering simulators, a planetarium, laboratories and a campus dormitory.

Degree programmes are offered in English, with a 9-month preparatory language course available. Military cadets are fully funded by the Ministry of Defence, while civilian tuition ranges from €2,750/year (EU) to €3,900/year (non-EU). Rector: Flotilla Admiral Prof. Kalin Kalinov.

5.name: Varna Free University
5.description: Bulgaria's largest private university — law, economics, IT, psychology, security and architecture by the Black Sea.
5.longDescription:
Varna Free University "Chernorizets Hrabar" (VFU) is the largest and most established private university in Bulgaria, founded in 1991 and granted full higher-education status in 1995. It is named after Chernorizets Hrabar, the medieval Bulgarian monk and writer. The university holds its third institutional accreditation from the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency (NEAA) for the maximum six-year period, with a score of 9.12 out of 10, and is an active member of the European University Association (EUA) with the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education, ECTS and Diploma Supplement labels and the HR Excellence in Research award.

The university is organised into three faculties — the Faculty of Social, Business and Computer Sciences (economics, administration and management, psychology, informatics and computer science), the Faculty of Law (law, national security and public order) and the Faculty of Architecture (architecture, construction engineering, fine arts, and music and dance) — together with a branch in Smolyan and a Department of Foreign Language Teaching and Postgraduate Qualification.

VFU offers more than 60 bachelor's and master's programmes and 29 doctoral programmes, taught in Bulgarian, English and Turkish, in full-time, part-time and distance-learning formats. Over the last three decades more than 30,000 students have graduated. The seaside campus in the Chayka resort features modern lecture halls and computer laboratories, a moot courtroom, design and architecture studios, a library, a Centre for Digital Technologies, a medical centre, sports facilities and student accommodation.

Tuition for Bulgarian and EU students ranges from about €848 to €1,354 per semester depending on the programme, while international (non-EU) students pay €1,600–€1,800 per semester for bachelor's and €1,800–€2,000 for master's programmes. Rector: Prof. Dr. Petar Hristov.

6.name: University of Management
6.description: International, English-taught business school in Varna offering dual Bulgarian–British (Cardiff Met) degrees in business, tourism, IT and culinary arts.
6.longDescription:
The University of Management (VUM) in Varna is an international business school and one of Bulgaria's most internationally recognised higher-education institutions. Founded in 1996 as a college of tourism and renamed from International College – Albena in 2015, it marks 30 years in 2026. Students from more than 45 countries study business, marketing, information technology and computer science, tourism, hotel management and culinary arts in a multicultural, English-language environment.

VUM is accredited by the Bulgarian National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency (NEAA) in the professional fields of Administration and Management, Economics, Tourism, Informatics and Computer Science, Pedagogy of Teaching and Food Technologies, and offers bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes through its Faculty of Business.

The university's flagship is its dual-diploma model: bachelor's and master's programmes are taught entirely in English and lead to both a Bulgarian VUM diploma and a British degree from strategic partner Cardiff Metropolitan University, without the usual requirement to spend a semester abroad. VUM also cooperates with University College Birmingham, Stenden University (Netherlands), the Business & Hotel Management School (Switzerland) and more than 100 institutions across Europe, Asia and South America.

VUM holds 4 Palmes of Excellence from Eduniversal, placing it among the world's top 200 business schools and making it the only Bulgarian institution at this level. It has been ranked No.1 in the world for student mobility by U-Multirank for four consecutive years; its Master in International Tourism is ranked 10th worldwide and its MBA 5th in Central and Eastern Europe by Eduniversal Best Masters. President: Assoc. Prof. Dr. Todor Radev. Rector: Prof. Dr. Krasimira Staneva.

7.name: Sofia University
7.description: Bulgaria's oldest and largest university (est. 1888) — a comprehensive research university in the heart of Sofia with 16 faculties spanning law, sciences, humanities, economics and medicine.
7.longDescription:
Sofia University "St. Kliment Ohridski" is the oldest and largest higher-education institution in Bulgaria, founded on 1 October 1888 and established as a university in 1904. Named after the medieval scholar St. Kliment Ohridski, it is the country's leading centre of teaching and research and is consistently ranked the No. 1 university in Bulgaria.

The university is organised into 16 faculties — Law, Philosophy, History, Classical and Modern Philology, Slavic Studies, Education, Educational Studies and the Arts, Journalism and Mass Communication, Theology, Economics and Business Administration, Mathematics and Informatics, Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy, Biology, Geology and Geography, and Medicine — together with three departments. It offers more than 100 bachelor's and over 200 master's programmes, plus doctoral training, in Bulgarian and in English and other foreign languages.

Today over 20,000 students study at the university, taught by around 1,700 academic staff. Its landmark Rectorate on Tsar Osvoboditel Boulevard — built between 1924 and 1934 with a donation from the brothers Evlogi and Hristo Georgiev — spans more than 18,000 m² with 324 rooms. The university also runs the largest university library in the country, a botanical garden, observatories and modern research institutes, including INSAIT, which won Bulgaria's first European Research Council grant.

Sofia University maintains a wide international network through Erasmus+, the Transform4Europe alliance and hundreds of bilateral agreements, and its alumni include Bulgarian presidents, prime ministers, academicians and cultural figures. Bulgarian and EU students study on state-subsidised or paid places, while foreign students pay tuition set per programme; Medicine and Pharmacy are also offered as English-taught degrees. Rector: Prof. Dr. Georgi Valchev.

8.name: Technical University of Sofia
8.description: Bulgaria's largest and foremost university for engineering and technology (est. 1945) — computing, electronics, electrical, mechanical and industrial engineering, with English, German and French-taught programs.
8.longDescription:
The Technical University of Sofia (TU-Sofia) is the largest and most prestigious higher school of engineering and technology in Bulgaria, founded on 15 October 1945 as the State Polytechnic and granted its current university status in 1995. It is the country's leading centre for training engineers and a founding member of the European University of Technology (EUt+) alliance.

The university is organised into 17 faculties based in Sofia, Plovdiv and Sliven, including specialised foreign-language faculties that teach engineering entirely in German (FDIBA), English (ELFE) and French. Its Sofia faculties cover Automation, Computer Systems and Technologies, Electronic Engineering, Telecommunications, Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Technology, Transport, Management, and Applied Mathematics and Informatics, together with two colleges and vocational schools.

TU-Sofia has around 11,000 students — some 8,800 bachelor's, 1,900 master's and 500 doctoral students — across a wide range of engineering, computing and management programmes, many delivered in partnership with leading technology companies. Facilities include a High-Technology Business Incubator and Technology Park, modern laboratories, a central scientific-technical library, a sports complex and student dormitories in the Studentski Grad campus.

The university maintains extensive international cooperation through the EUt+ alliance, Erasmus+ and hundreds of partnerships, and works closely with industry — Bosch, SAP, VMware, Festo, Siemens and others — which sponsor scholarships, laboratories and internships. Bulgarian and EU students study on state-subsidised or paid places, while foreign students can study in Bulgarian, English, German or French. Rector: Prof. Dr. Georgi Venkov.

9.name: University of National and World Economy
9.description: Bulgaria's oldest and largest university of economics and business (est. 1920) — economics, finance, management, informatics, international relations and law, in the heart of Sofia.
9.longDescription:
The University of National and World Economy (UNWE) is the oldest and largest higher school of economics and business in Bulgaria and South-Eastern Europe, founded in 1920 as the Free University of Political and Economic Sciences. After several transformations it took its present name in 1990 and is today the country's leading centre for economic, business and administrative education, ranked first in Bulgaria in its professional fields.

The university is organised into 8 faculties — General Economics, Finance and Accountancy, Business, Economics of Infrastructure, Management and Administration, International Economics and Politics, Applied Informatics and Statistics, and Law. It offers 53 bachelor's, 90 master's and 45 doctoral programmes, including majors taught entirely in English, and holds the highest institutional accreditation from the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency.

UNWE has around 20,000 students on its campus in the Studentski Grad district of Sofia. The 41,000 m² complex features 120 auditoriums and 367 study rooms, a modern library, an inter-university Career Development Centre, sports facilities and student dormitories for nearly 5,000 students.

The university is a member of the ENGAGE.EU European University alliance and cooperates with 187 international and 221 local partners through Erasmus+ and joint programmes. Its alumni include five Bulgarian prime ministers, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and many leading economists and public figures. Bulgarian and EU students study on state-subsidised or paid places, while foreign students can study in Bulgarian or English. Rector: Prof. Dr. Dimitar Dimitrov.

10.name: Medical University of Sofia
10.description: Bulgaria's oldest and most prestigious medical university (est. 1917) — medicine, dental medicine, pharmacy and public health, with English-taught programs and 14 university hospitals.
10.longDescription:
The Medical University of Sofia (MU-Sofia) is the oldest and largest institution for higher medical education in Bulgaria, founded on 22 November 1917 as the Medical Faculty of Sofia University and later made an independent university, adopting its present name in 1995. It is the country's leading centre for medical education, science and healthcare and is accredited with the highest rating by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency.

The university comprises four faculties — Medicine, Dental Medicine, Pharmacy and Public Health "Prof. Dr. Tsekomir Vodenicharov" — together with the Medical College "Yordanka Filaretova", a Department for Language Training and Sport and a branch in Vratsa. It has around 8,300 students, including some 800 international students from Germany, Greece, the UK, Italy, Scandinavia, Switzerland, the Middle East and India, and about 120 doctoral candidates.

MU-Sofia trains doctors, dentists, pharmacists and public-health specialists across integrated Master's, professional bachelor and doctoral programmes. Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy are also offered entirely in English for international students. Clinical training takes place in 14 university hospitals, including the historic Alexandrovska Hospital, supported by modern simulation centres, research laboratories and libraries.

The university maintains active Erasmus+ and bilateral cooperation across Europe and beyond and is ranked among the region's leading medical schools. Bulgarian and EU students study on state-subsidised or paid places, while foreign students in the English-taught programmes pay tuition set per programme. Rector: Prof. Dr. Boycho Landzhov.

11.name: New Bulgarian University
11.description: One of Bulgaria's leading private, liberal-arts universities (est. 1991) — business, economics, law, informatics, design, arts, psychology and social sciences in Sofia.
11.longDescription:
New Bulgarian University (NBU) is one of the first and most prestigious private universities in Bulgaria, founded on 18 September 1991 by Prof. Bogdan Bogdanov and a group of Bulgarian intellectuals through a resolution of the National Assembly. It pioneered liberal education, the credit (ECTS) system, interdisciplinary study and distance learning in Bulgaria, with the mission of modernising Bulgarian higher education.

The university is organised into more than 24 departments rather than classic faculties, spanning economics, business and administration, law, informatics and telecommunications, design and architecture, fine arts, cinema, theatre and music, psychology and cognitive science, political science, mass communications and the humanities. It offers 54 bachelor's, around 100 master's and 35 doctoral programmes, including tracks taught in English.

NBU has around 12,000 students on its campus in the Ovcha Kupel district of western Sofia, near Vitosha mountain. The campus comprises two main buildings with over 100 halls, computer laboratories, design and film studios, theatres and sports facilities, and an award-winning academic library holding over 128,000 items. The Central and East European Center for Cognitive Science is a distinctive research hub.

The university is accredited by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency, is an accredited provider of The Open University Business School (UK), and maintains a wide Erasmus+ and international network; its honorary doctors include Richard Rorty, Julia Kristeva and Geert Hofstede. As a private university, NBU is tuition-based, with fees paid per semester that remain unchanged for the whole study period and a range of family, social and alumni discounts. Rector: Prof. Dr. Plamen Doynov.

12.name: University of Architecture, Civil Engineering and Geodesy
12.description: Bulgaria's only specialised state university for architecture, civil engineering and geodesy (est. 1942) — architecture, structural, hydraulic, transport engineering and geodesy in Sofia.
12.longDescription:
The University of Architecture, Civil Engineering and Geodesy (UACEG) is Bulgaria's oldest and only specialised state university for architecture, construction and geodesy, established in 1942 and made an independent higher school in 1945. It is the country's leading centre for training architects, civil engineers, geodesists and urban planners, accredited with a high rating by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency.

The university is organised into five faculties — Architecture, Structural Engineering, Hydraulic Engineering, Transportation Engineering and Geodesy — with 33 departments covering architecture, urbanism, building and structural construction, water supply and sewerage, transport construction, hydro-engineering and geodesy. It has around 5,000 students and offers integrated Master's, bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes, including Architecture and Civil Engineering taught in English for international students.

UACEG's campus is on Hristo Smirnenski Boulevard in central Sofia, with design studios, engineering and materials-testing laboratories, a large scientific-technical library, computer halls, a sports complex and student dormitories. Its diploma is FEANI-recognised and the university appears in the QS Emerging Europe & Central Asia rankings.

The university maintains a wide Erasmus+ and bilateral network and close ties with the construction and design industry. Bulgarian and EU students study on state-subsidised or paid places (about €215 per semester subsidised), while foreign students in the English-taught Architecture and Civil Engineering programmes pay tuition set per programme. Rector: Prof. Dr. Arch. Gichka Kutova-Kamenova.

13.name: University of Chemical Technology and Metallurgy
13.description: Bulgaria's leading specialised university for chemical technology, metallurgy and materials science (est. 1953) — chemistry, biotechnology, metallurgy, environmental and industrial engineering in Sofia, with English, French and German-taught programs.
13.longDescription:
The University of Chemical Technology and Metallurgy (UCTM) is Bulgaria's leading specialised state university for chemical engineering, chemical technology, metallurgy and materials science, established in 1953 as the Institute of Chemical Technology. It holds the highest institutional accreditation in the country for its professional field and its engineering specialties are recognised by FEANI (the European Federation of National Engineering Associations).

The university is organised into three faculties — Chemical Technologies, Chemical and Systems Engineering, and Metallurgy and Materials Science — together with a Francophone Faculty of Chemical Engineering. Its departments cover chemical and biochemical technology, biotechnology, polymers, pharmaceutical and fine chemistry, metallurgy, materials and nanomaterials, electrochemistry, environmental engineering, automation, information technology and industrial management.

UCTM has around 3,800 students in bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes, taught in Bulgarian and — for many programmes — in English, French and German. It offers European double-diploma engineering degrees jointly with partner universities such as Hamburg and Otto von Guericke Magdeburg.

The campus in Sofia's Studentski Grad district features modern chemical, metallurgical and materials laboratories, pilot installations, a scientific-technical library, computer halls, a sports complex and student dormitories. Bulgarian and EU students study on state-subsidised or paid places (from about €430 per year), while foreign students in the foreign-language programmes pay tuition from about €4,600 per year. Rector: Prof. Dr. Eng. Senia Terzieva.

14.name: University of Mining and Geology "St. Ivan Rilski"
14.description: Bulgaria's only specialised university for mining, geology and earth sciences (est. 1953) — mining, geology, geophysics, oil & gas, electromechanics and environmental engineering in Sofia.
14.longDescription:
The University of Mining and Geology "St. Ivan Rilski" (MGU) is Bulgaria's only specialised state university for mining, geology and the earth sciences, established on 10 June 1953. Named after St. Ivan Rilski, the patron of Bulgarian miners and geologists, it is the country's leading centre for training engineers in geological exploration, mining, oil and gas, and mineral resources, and is accredited by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency.

The university is organised into three faculties — Mining Technology, Mining Electromechanics, and Geology and Exploration — with a Humanitarian Department. Its departments cover mineral-resource development, underground construction, mine surveying, mineral processing and recycling, blasting technologies, electromechanics and automation, mining machinery, geology and geoinformatics, geophysics, hydrogeology and engineering geology, geoecology, and drilling, oil and gas production.

Since its founding MGU has trained over 14,000 engineers who work in geology, mining, energy, construction and environmental protection worldwide. It has around 2,000 students in bachelor's (4 years), master's and doctoral programmes, with a main campus in Sofia's Studentski Grad district and a branch in Kardzhali.

The campus features specialised mining, geology and materials laboratories, a rich mineralogical and geological museum, a scientific-technical library, computer halls, a sports complex and student dormitories, and the university works closely with the mining and energy industry, which sponsors scholarships and internships. Bulgarian and EU students study on state-subsidised or paid places (from about €430 per year), while foreign students pay tuition set per programme. Rector: Prof. Dr. Eng. Ivaylo Koprev.

15.name: University of Forestry
15.description: Bulgaria's only university for forestry, ecology and landscape architecture (est. 1925) — forestry, wood technology, veterinary medicine, agronomy, landscape architecture and business in Sofia.
15.longDescription:
The University of Forestry (LTU) is Bulgaria's oldest and only specialised state university for forestry, forest management, landscape architecture and wood technology, with roots dating to 1925 when a Forestry Division was founded at Sofia University. It became an independent higher school in 1953 and took its present name in 1995, and it is accredited by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency under the motto "Bulgarian traditions and European standards in education".

The university is organised into six faculties — Forestry, Forest Industry, Ecology and Landscape Architecture, Agronomy, Veterinary Medicine, and Business Management — with around 30 departments. In the 1990s it broadened from forestry, wood processing and landscape architecture to also cover ecology, agronomy, veterinary medicine and business.

LTU offers bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes on the European credit system. It is the only university in Sofia teaching Veterinary Medicine in English, and it welcomes international students across several fields. Practical training is supported by two university research forests near Yundola and Barzia and a training facility in the Vrazhdebna area.

The wooded campus in central Sofia features specialised forestry, wood, agronomy and veterinary laboratories, a veterinary clinic, an arboretum and botanical collections, a scientific library, a sports complex and student dormitories. Bulgarian and EU students study on state-subsidised or paid places (from about €430 per year), while foreign students pay tuition set per programme. Rector: Prof. Dr. Ivan Iliev.

16.name: University of Library Studies and Information Technologies
16.description: Bulgaria's specialised state university for information technologies, library science and cultural heritage (est. 1950) — from computer science, cybersecurity and AI to archives, media and national security, in Sofia.
16.longDescription:
The University of Library Studies and Information Technologies (ULSIT, known as UniBIT) is Bulgaria's specialised state university for information science, library and archival studies, cultural heritage and information technologies. It was founded in 1950 as the State Institute of Library Studies, grew from an institute into a college, became a Specialised Higher School in 2004, and was granted full university status by the National Assembly in 2010.

UniBIT is organised into two faculties — the Faculty of Library Studies and Cultural Heritage and the Faculty of Information Sciences — supported by a department of comprehensive studies, five research institutes and specialised laboratories and centres. Around 2,500 Bulgarian and international students study across bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes, taught by more than 140 lecturers. The rector is Prof. Dr. Irena Peteva.

The university combines its traditional strengths in library science, archives, publishing and cultural heritage with fast-growing programmes in computer science, information technology, information and cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, software engineering and national security. It holds a UNESCO Chair, is a member of the Balkan Universities Network, and is institutionally accredited by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency.

The Sofia campus offers a modern Library and Information Centre with 52,000 volumes and international databases, ten computer rooms and the "John Atanasoff" computer laboratory, a sports complex and dormitories in Studentski Grad. Bulgarian and EU students study at low state-subsidised fees of about €530 per year, while foreign students pay around €4,600 per year; the Software Engineering master's is also offered in English.

17.name: Todor Kableshkov University of Transport
17.description: Bulgaria's specialised state university for transport (est. 1922) — railway, automotive and transport engineering, telecommunications, electrical equipment, logistics and transport management, in Sofia.
17.longDescription:
Todor Kableshkov University of Transport (VTU) is Bulgaria's specialised state university for transport, and one of the country's oldest engineering-technical higher schools. It was founded in 1922 as the State Railway School and, over more than a century, has grown into a modern university under the motto "Traditions and professional knowledge", training engineers and managers for the whole transport sector.

The university is organised into three faculties — Transport Management, Machinery and Construction Technologies in Transport, and Telecommunications and Electrical Equipment in Transport. Around 2,500 students study across bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes, taught by more than 160 lecturers, and VTU counts over 30,000 alumni. The rector is Prof. Dr. Eng. Daniela Todorova.

Programmes span railway and automotive engineering, rolling stock, transport construction, hoisting and construction machinery, electric transport and electric vehicles, telecommunications and signalling, transport economics, logistics, accounting and industrial management. VTU was among the first Bulgarian universities to enrol students directly into master's programmes and is institutionally accredited by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency.

The campus in Sofia's Slatina district (158 Geo Milev Street) has specialised transport laboratories including a Road Safety Laboratory, a transport museum, a library, dormitories and a Black Sea recreation centre at Ravda. Bulgarian and EU students study at low state-subsidised fees (from about €300 per year, with full exemptions for certain categories), while foreign students pay around €3,000 per year.

18.name: University of Telecommunications and Post
18.description: Bulgaria's oldest telecommunications and IT higher school (est. 1881) — telecommunications, computer technologies, cybersecurity, AI, digital entrepreneurship and management, in Sofia.
18.longDescription:
The University of Telecommunications and Post (UTP) is a specialised state higher school in Sofia and the institution with the longest history in Bulgaria after the Military School. It traces its origins to the State Telegraph-Postal School founded by decree of Prince Alexander I on 21 December 1881, became the College of Telecommunications and Posts in 1997 and gained higher-school status in 2015, marking 145 years in 2026.

UTP is built around its Faculty of Telecommunications and Management and is accredited in the professional fields of Communication & Computer Technology and Administration & Management. Around 1,500 students study across professional-bachelor, bachelor, master's and doctoral programmes, under the motto "Wisdom, Knowledge, Competence". The rector is Prof. Dr. Miglena Temelkova.

Programmes focus on telecommunications, computer technologies, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, digital entrepreneurship, digital public administration and management — including hybrid programmes in telemedicine and software programming in medicine run with the Medical Universities of Pleven and Plovdiv. Nearly 90% of students are employed in their field before graduation, and the school works closely with industry partners such as A1, Huawei, Siemens, Cisco and AWS.

The campus in Sofia's Studentski grad (1 Akademik Stefan Mladenov Street) offers modern telecommunications, networking and cybersecurity laboratories, a Cisco Networking Academy and AWS Academy, an e-learning platform and renovated dormitories. Bulgarian and EU students study at low fees (from about €360 per year, with exemptions for certain categories), while foreign students — from Serbia, North Macedonia, Turkey, Albania, Moldova and Ukraine — pay around €2,900 per year.

19.name: University of Insurance and Finance (VUZF)
19.description: Bulgaria's first private university for finance, insurance and business (est. 2002) — finance, fintech, insurance, accounting, management, marketing and digital business, in Sofia.
19.longDescription:
The University of Insurance and Finance (VUZF), also known as VUZF University, is Bulgaria's first private higher school specialised in finance, insurance, social insurance, management and marketing. It was established by a resolution of the National Assembly in 2002 and welcomed its first students in the 2002/2003 academic year, and today it is consistently ranked among the top three institutions in Bulgaria in the field of Economics.

VUZF teaches bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes in the professional field of Economics, organised around departments of Finance, Insurance and Social Security, Accounting and Control, and Management and Marketing. The rector is Prof. Boris Velchev, and the university was founded by its President and Rector Emeritus, Assoc. Prof. Dr. Grigorii Vazov. About 90% of graduates start work in their field — in banks, insurers, financial institutions and companies.

The curriculum emphasises practical, career-focused education delivered by working professionals, with a strong modern focus on fintech, digital finance, accounting and analytics, and green and sustainable economics. Several programmes are taught in English — including Business Management and Marketing and International Banking and Finance — and accounting degrees are accredited by ACCA. The university holds accreditation from both the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency and the British Accreditation Council.

The campus in Sofia's Ovcha Kupel district (1 Gusla Street) houses the VUZF Lab research centre, a specialised library, lecture halls and a Moodle e-learning platform for distance study. As a private university, VUZF charges per-semester fees — from about €1,000 for Bulgarian-taught programmes to €1,800–€3,410 for English-taught ones — with merit scholarships, discounts and instalment plans available.

20.name: National Sports Academy "Vasil Levski"
20.description: Bulgaria's national state university for sport, physical education and kinesitherapy (est. 1942) — coaching in around 60 sports, PE teaching, sports management, kinesitherapy and rehabilitation, in Sofia.
20.longDescription:
The National Sports Academy "Vasil Levski" (NSA) is Bulgaria's only specialised state university for sport, physical education and kinesitherapy (physiotherapy). It was founded in 1942 by decree of Tsar Boris III as the Higher School for Physical Education, became the Higher Institute for Physical Education and Sports in 1953, and took its present name in 1995. It has a strong Olympic heritage, and its alumni include many Olympic and world champions, coaches and national-team specialists.

Around 3,500 students study across three faculties — Sports, Pedagogy, and Public Health, Health Care and Tourism — plus a department of language education and information technologies. The Faculty of Sports trains coaches across roughly 60 sports disciplines, the Faculty of Pedagogy prepares physical-education teachers, and the health faculty educates kinesitherapists, ergotherapists and sports-animation specialists. The rector is Prof. Krasimir Petkov.

NSA offers bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes covering coaching, sports management, physical education, adapted physical activity, sports journalism, kinesitherapy, sports psychology, sports medicine and rehabilitation, and more. Admission is competitive and usually includes a practical aptitude examination alongside secondary-school results, and several programmes — including Kinesitherapy — are offered in English for international students.

The campus in Sofia's Studentski grad, with views of Mount Vitosha, offers stadiums, sports halls, an athletics track, a swimming pool and tennis courts, an Educational and Olympic Centre, the Centre for Scientific and Applied Activities in Sports, kinesitherapy clinics and student dormitories. Bulgarian and EU students pay affordable state fees — about €1,230 per year for sport and pedagogy specialties and €1,340 for Kinesitherapy — while foreign students pay around €3,300 per year.

21.name: VSU "Lyuben Karavelov"
21.description: Bulgaria's specialised state university for civil engineering and architecture (est. 1938) — construction of buildings, construction management, fire safety, architecture and the unique engineer-architect degree, in Sofia.
21.longDescription:
VSU "Lyuben Karavelov" (the Higher School of Civil Engineering "Lyuben Karavelov") is a specialised state university in Sofia for civil engineering and architecture. It was founded in 1938 as a military engineering school for Bulgaria's Construction Troops and became a civilian higher school in 2000; a Faculty of Architecture was added in 2006. It still trains both civilian and military students, under the motto "Vision. Construction. Success".

The university is organised into two faculties — Civil Engineering and Architecture — teaching in the professional field of Architecture, Construction and Geodesy. Around 1,000 students study bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes with about 99 lecturers, and the rector is Assoc. Prof. Dr. Eng. Iliyana Stoynova. VSU is institutionally accredited by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency.

Programmes cover construction of buildings and facilities, construction management (also taught in English), fire safety and rescue, architecture, and the combined "engineer-architect" degree that is unique in Bulgaria. Master's specialisations include building constructions, construction technology and management, investment project management, urbanism, design, and architectural heritage preservation — the last offered only at VSU.

VSU has its own student campus in south-west Sofia (175 Suhodolska Street), with construction and structural-testing laboratories, architecture and design studios, a specialised library, dormitories and sports facilities. Bulgarian and EU students pay affordable state fees from about €430 per year (around €700 for architecture and paid programmes), while foreign students pay around €3,000 per year.

22.name: National Academy of Art
22.description: Bulgaria's oldest and most prestigious art academy (est. 1896 as the State Drawing School) — painting, sculpture, graphics, scenography, restoration, ceramics, fashion and design, in Sofia.
22.longDescription:
The National Academy of Art (NHA) is Bulgaria's oldest and most prestigious institution of fine and applied arts. It was founded on 1 October 1896 as the State Drawing School and grew into a full academy; its landmark red-brick building at 1 Shipka Street in central Sofia was built in 1907. Its alumni include many of Bulgaria's leading artists, sculptors, designers and art scholars.

Around 1,000 students study across two faculties — Fine Arts and Applied Arts and Design — with more than 50 international students and over 50 doctoral candidates. The academy offers about two dozen specialties in visual arts, art studies and design, and the rector is Prof. Georgi Yankov. NHA also has a branch in Burgas and creative residences on the Black Sea coast.

Programmes span painting, mural painting, sculpture, graphics, book and print graphics, poster and visual communication, scenography, conservation and restoration, art studies, ceramics, textile art, fashion, industrial and advertising design, and photography. Admission is by competitive creative examinations — drawing, composition and specialty tasks — and a portfolio, at both bachelor's and master's level.

The historic Shipka Street building houses studios and workshops for each specialty, the Academia Gallery and exhibition halls, and the academy stages hundreds of student shows, fashion shows and public art events every year. Annual tuition for 2025/2026 is about €2,308, paid in two semester instalments, with foreign students paying around €3,500; NHA is active in Erasmus+ and partners with academies such as the China Academy of Art.

23.name: National Academy of Music
23.description: Bulgaria's only state academy for professional musicians (est. 1921, named after Prof. Pancho Vladigerov) — instrumental and vocal performance, composition, conducting, musicology, music pedagogy, folk music, pop & jazz and ballet, in Sofia.
23.longDescription:
The National Academy of Music "Prof. Pancho Vladigerov" (NMA) is the only higher-education institution in Bulgaria dedicated entirely to professional musicians, covering the full range of music-theoretical and performance specialties. It was founded on 21 July 1921 by Royal Decree as the State Music Academy — growing out of the private music school opened in 1904 — and in 2006 was elevated to a National Academy. It is named after the composer and pianist Prof. Pancho Vladigerov.

Around 800 students study across three faculties — Theory, Composition and Conducting; Instrumental; and Vocal (which also covers ballet art and pop & jazz) — and the rector is Prof. Dr. Sava Dimitrov. The academy teaches over 30 specialties at bachelor's, master's and doctoral level, and its distinguished teachers have included Dobri Hristov, Pancho Vladigerov, Lyubomir Pipkov and Marin Goleminov.

Programmes span piano, string, wind and percussion instruments, accordion and classical guitar, classical, chamber and pop & jazz singing, composition, opera-symphony and choral conducting, musicology, music pedagogy, Bulgarian folk music, ballet, sound engineering, music and stage direction, and the management of music and performing arts. Admission is by competitive practical examinations in the chosen specialty.

The academy has its own academic symphony orchestra, choir and teaching opera theatre, a specialised music library with rare editions and a sound archive, and concert halls at its two Sofia buildings on Boulevard "Evlogi i Hristo Georgievi" and Lyudmil Stoyanov Street. Bulgarian and EU students on state-funded places pay low annual fees from about €450 (music pedagogy) to €850, with a 50% refund on each successfully completed year, while foreign students pay around €7,000-€8,500 per year. NMA is active in Erasmus+ and its graduates win top prizes at international competitions.

24.name: Rakovski National Defence College
24.description: Bulgaria's oldest and only state military academy (est. 1912, named after Georgi Stoykov Rakovski) — national security and defence, strategic leadership, command and staff, cybersecurity and defence management, in Sofia.
24.longDescription:
The Rakovski National Defence College — officially the Military Academy "Georgi Stoykov Rakovski" — is Bulgaria's oldest and most senior military higher-education institution, and the third-oldest higher school in the country. It was established by decree on 1 March 1912 as the country's first higher military school, opened in 1915 after the Balkan Wars, and was named in 1946 after Georgi Stoykov Rakovski, a leader of the Bulgarian national-liberation movement.

The academy trains both military officers and civilians in the field of security and defence, and is led by its commandant, Major General Stayko Prokopiev. It is organised into two faculties — National Security and Defence, and Command and Staff — together with a Department of Language Training and the Defence Advanced Research Institute (DARI). Teaching and research cover the professional fields of National Security, Military Science and Psychology.

The college offers accredited programmes at bachelor's, master's and doctoral level. Bachelor's studies are in Security and Defence and in Cybersecurity, while its sixteen master's specialties span strategic leadership of defence and the armed forces, command and staff, security and defence management, corporate and aviation security, counter-terrorism, protection of the population and critical infrastructure, industrial, energy and climate security, logistics, cybersecurity, communication and information systems, and psychology in security and defence.

Serving military students are funded by the Ministry of Defence and study without tuition, while civilian students may enrol in state-subsidised or paid places (paid civilian fees are around €360-€770 per year, with foreign students paying about €3,000). The academy is active in NATO cooperation and Erasmus+, holds strong national accreditation (9.02/10), and hosts the Defence Advanced Research Institute and its "Voenen Zhurnal" journal on a historic campus on Boulevard "Evlogi i Hristo Georgievi" in central Sofia.

25.name: National Academy of Theatre and Film Arts
25.description: Bulgaria's first and most prestigious theatre and film school (est. 1948, named after Krastyo Sarafov) — acting, directing, dramaturgy, scenography, film and TV, cinematography, animation and arts management, in Sofia.
25.longDescription:
The National Academy of Theatre and Film Arts "Krastyo Sarafov" (NATFA) is Bulgaria's first and most prestigious higher school of stage and screen arts. Founded in 1948 as the country's first higher theatre school, it is named after the celebrated actor Krastyo Sarafov, and its history is closely bound up with the development of Bulgarian theatre and cinema. Its alumni include many of Bulgaria's leading actors, directors, cinematographers and playwrights.

About 220 students are admitted each year across two faculties — Stage Arts and Screen Arts — and the rector is Prof. DSc Miroslav Dachev. The academy has been a full member of CILECT (the International Association of Film and Television Schools) since 1982 and of ELIA (the European League of Institutes of the Arts) since 1990, and takes part in the FilmEU alliance.

Programmes span drama and puppet-theatre acting, movement and dance theatre, performing-arts directing, scenography, theatre studies, management and production, film and TV directing, cinematography, editing, sound, producing and design, screenwriting and playwriting, photography, animation and screen research, with master's specialties in directing, screenwriting, animation, photographic art and arts management. Admission is by competitive creative examinations — auditions, screen tests, portfolios and specialty tasks.

NATFA is built around working stages — the NATFA Theatre and NATFA Puppet Theatre — and an Educational Audio-visual Complex with film and TV studios, plus a specialised library, dormitory and canteen. Bulgarian and EU students pay affordable state fees (about €920 per year for bachelor's and €1,020 for master's), while foreign students pay around €4,000 per year for stage arts and €6,000 for film and TV. The academy is active in Erasmus+ and its student films and productions travel to international festivals.

26.name: Academy of the Ministry of the Interior
26.description: Bulgaria's state academy for police, security and fire-safety officers (police education since 1879, university status 2002) — counteraction to crime, national security, border police, public administration and fire safety, in Sofia.
26.longDescription:
The Academy of the Ministry of the Interior (Academy of the MoI) is Bulgaria's specialised state higher-education institution for police, security and fire-safety professionals. Its lineage goes back to the police-administrative department founded in 1879, through the Higher Special School and the Higher Institute (VIPOND); it gained university status as the "Academy of the Ministry of the Interior" in 2002. It trains civil servants for the Ministry of the Interior and specialists for other law-enforcement and security bodies.

The Academy is organised into two faculties — Police, and Fire Safety and Civil Protection — together with a Scientific Research Institute and a Centre for Vocational Training, and is led by its rector, Senior Commissioner Assoc. Prof. Dr. Milorad Yordanov. Its campus is in the Mladost district of Sofia (1 Aleksandar Malinov Blvd), on the historic former grounds of the American College.

The Academy offers accredited bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes in the professional fields of national security and law. Bachelor's specialties include counteraction to crime and public order, border police, protection of national security, public administration, and fire safety and protection of the population, while master's specialties add strategic management of security and public order, psychological support for operational-investigative activities, and fire and emergency safety.

Cadets study on a fully Ministry-of-Interior-funded basis — four years of tuition-free education, guaranteed accommodation and a state-guaranteed stipend for the whole course, followed by appointment in the Ministry of the Interior. Civilian students may enrol in state-subsidised or paid places (paid civilian fees are around €360-€640 per year, with foreign students paying about €3,000). The Academy takes part in Erasmus+ and CEPOL cooperation and works closely with the structures of the Ministry of the Interior.

27.name: Luben Groys Theatre College
27.description: Bulgaria's first private higher theatre school (est. 1991, named after director Luben Groys) — a specialised college training professional-bachelor actors for drama theatre and for film, in Sofia.
27.longDescription:
The Luben Groys Theatre College is Bulgaria's first private higher theatre school. It was founded in 1991 and is named after the celebrated Bulgarian theatre director Luben Groys (1934-1982), a graduate of the National Academy of Theatre and Film Arts. The college is dedicated entirely to training actors and holds programme accreditation from the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency.

It is the only higher-education institution in Bulgaria that offers a three-year "professional bachelor" degree in acting, in the professional field of Theatre and Film Art. Teaching is organised around small, intensive studios led by leading theatre and film professionals, and the rector is Prof. Dr. Stefan Serezliev.

The college offers two acting specialisations — Acting for Drama Theatre, led by the acclaimed director Liliya Abadjieva, and Acting for Film, led by the actor and producer Bashar Rahal. Both are three-year programmes of six semesters built around practical stage and screen work, culminating in public productions and screen projects.

Admission is by a competitive creative examination in three rounds — candidates present poetry, a fable, a prose excerpt, two contrasting monologues, a song and a dance. Tuition is about €1,365 per semester (around €2,730 per year), plus small registration and exam fees. The college is based in central Sofia on George Washington Street.

28.name: MT&M College
28.description: Sofia's private 'Danish College' (est. 1993 via a Denmark-Bulgaria agreement) — a professional-bachelor college specialising in marketing, advertising, digital marketing and entrepreneurship, with an AI-in-business focus.
28.longDescription:
MT&M College — the College of Management, Trade and Marketing — is a private higher-education college in Sofia, widely known as "the Danish College". It was founded in 1993 under an intergovernmental agreement between the Kingdom of Denmark and the Republic of Bulgaria, and in 2001 the National Assembly gave it the status of an autonomous college awarding the "professional bachelor" degree. It is accredited by the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency.

The college specialises in marketing, advertising, trade and entrepreneurship, and describes its education as flexible, digital and practical. Over its three decades it has taught more than 9,000 graduates, with students from some 35 countries, and it keeps close links with its Danish partner college in Roskilde. Its curriculum now includes innovative subjects on the use of Artificial Intelligence in business.

Studies lead to a three-year professional bachelor's degree, with specialisations in Marketing (offered since 1993) and Entrepreneurship (since 2013), alongside tracks in advertising and communications, digital marketing and international marketing. Teaching combines micro- and macroeconomics, statistics, finance, accounting, commercial law and foreign languages with hands-on, project-based work.

Admission is open to all secondary-school graduates, with autumn and spring intakes and full-time and part-time study; selection is by an aptitude test, an English placement test and a motivation interview. Tuition is moderate for a private college (around €1,300 per year for Bulgarian and EU students, higher for international students). The college is based in central Sofia at the Prima Business Center.

29.name: South-West University "Neofit Rilski"
29.description: Blagoevgrad's large public university (est. 1975) — a classical, comprehensive university with nine faculties spanning law, economics, philology, philosophy, pedagogy, sciences, public health and sport, arts and engineering.
29.longDescription:
South-West University "Neofit Rilski" is a state university in Blagoevgrad, in the heart of south-west Bulgaria between the Rila and Pirin mountains. It was founded in 1975 as a branch of Sofia University, became an independent Higher Pedagogical Institute in 1983 and was granted full university status by the National Assembly in 1995. It is named after Neofit Rilski, the "patriarch of modern Bulgarian education".

Today it is one of the country's leading classical, comprehensive universities, with around 12,500 students and some 470 academic staff. Its structure includes nine faculties — Law and History, Economics, Philology, Philosophy, Pedagogy, Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Public Health, Health Care and Sport, Arts, and the Technical (Engineering) Faculty — together with a department for language training and continuing education.

The university offers a very broad academic portfolio: roughly 71 bachelor's, 100 master's and more than 70 doctoral programmes across the humanities, social and natural sciences, health, sport, the arts and engineering. Its Faculty of Arts is unique in Bulgaria, teaching music, fine arts, fashion, choreography, theatre and film alongside cultural studies and cultural tourism, while the Faculty of Public Health, Health Care and Sport prepares nurses, midwives, kinesitherapists and speech therapists.

Study is mainly in Bulgarian, with selected programmes and courses in English and a one-year Bulgarian-language preparatory course for international students. Admission is by state matriculation results or university entrance exams, in several competitive rounds. Tuition is among the lowest at any Bulgarian state university — roughly €150–€260 per semester for Bulgarian and EU students on state-subsidised places — and a wide range of merit, social and Erasmus+ scholarships is available.

30.name: American University in Bulgaria
30.description: Blagoevgrad's private American-style liberal-arts university (est. 1991) — the first of its kind in Eastern Europe, taught entirely in English, US- and Bulgarian-accredited, with students from 40+ countries.
30.longDescription:
The American University in Bulgaria (AUBG) is a private, American-style liberal-arts university in Blagoevgrad, in south-west Bulgaria. Founded in 1991 as a cooperative venture supported by the United States and Bulgarian governments, the Open Society Institute, the City of Blagoevgrad and the University of Maine, it was the first American-style liberal-arts university in Eastern Europe. Its first class in 1991 had just 208 students; today it has around 1,200 students from more than 40 countries across five continents, and its president is J.D. Mininger.

AUBG is accredited both in the United States, by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE), and in Bulgaria, and its degrees are recognised across the EU. All programmes are taught entirely in English, and students graduate with a US-style Bachelor of Arts. More than 60% complete a double major or a major-and-minor combination, reflecting the breadth of the liberal-arts model.

Students choose from 13 majors, 20 minors and several concentrations across departments in business and economics, computer science, politics and European studies, journalism and mass communication, literature and modern languages, and mathematics and science. AUBG's Business Administration, Journalism and Mass Communication, Political Science and International Relations and European Studies programmes are consistently ranked first in Bulgaria. At graduate level the university runs an Executive MBA in Sofia.

The campus combines a landmark Main Building on Blagoevgrad's central square with the modern Skaptopara campus, home to the Balkanski Academic Center, three residence halls, the ABF Sports Hall, the America for Bulgaria Student Center and the Panitza Library — the largest English-language library in South-East Europe. As a private university, AUBG charges US-style tuition (around €13,800 per year), but supports students with extensive merit- and need-based aid. Its alumni — more than 13,000 in over 100 countries — include entrepreneurs, journalists and public figures such as investigative reporter Christo Grozev and Sofia mayor Vassil Terziev.

31.name: College of Tourism – Blagoevgrad
31.description: Blagoevgrad's private, specialised tourism college (est. 2003) — a NEAA-accredited professional-bachelor school for hotel and restaurant management, tourist services and business administration.
31.longDescription:
The College of Tourism – Blagoevgrad (COTUR) is a private, specialised higher-education college in the centre of Blagoevgrad, in south-west Bulgaria. It was founded on 16 October 2003 and is dedicated to training professionals for the tourism, hospitality and travel industry — one of the region's most important economic sectors. In February 2025 it received a fresh institutional accreditation from the National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency (NEAA), valid until 2031.

The college awards the 'professional bachelor' degree — a practical, three-year higher-education qualification — across two professional fields: Tourism (3.9) and Administration and Management (3.7). Its specialties are Organization and Management of Hotels and Restaurants, Organization and Management of Tourist Services, Tourist Animation and Tour Guiding, and Business Administration, offered in both full-time and part-time forms.

Teaching combines classroom study with a strong emphasis on practice: students train in service, hospitality, tourism operations and management, and complete internships in partner hotels, restaurants and tour operators. A Moodle-based e-learning platform supports distance and blended learning, and the college takes part in Erasmus+ mobility for study and traineeships across Europe.

As a private college, COTUR charges moderate tuition (indicatively around €700–€750 per year for full-time study, lower for part-time), and supports students through national scholarship schemes, Erasmus+ grants and flexible payment. Based in a renovated building at 2 Bregalnitsa Street, it offers a focused, career-oriented route into the hotel, restaurant and tourism professions.

32.name: University of Plovdiv "Paisii Hilendarski"
32.description: Plovdiv's large public university (est. 1961) — the biggest in southern Bulgaria and second-largest in the country, a classical, comprehensive university with nine faculties across the sciences, humanities, economics and law.
32.longDescription:
The University of Plovdiv "Paisii Hilendarski" is a state university in Plovdiv, the second city of Bulgaria. It was founded in 1961 as the Higher Pedagogical Institute of Natural Sciences and was granted full university status in 1972, taking the name of Paisii Hilendarski, the monk-historian who helped spark the Bulgarian National Revival. Today it is the largest university in southern Bulgaria and the second-largest in the country, with around 18,000–20,000 students and some 560 academic staff; its rector is Prof. Dr. Rumen Mladenov.

The university is organised into nine faculties — Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Technology, Mathematics and Informatics, Economic and Social Sciences, Law, Philology, Philosophy and History, and Pedagogy — together with branches in Smolyan and Kardzhali and a technical college in Smolyan. Although it began as a natural-sciences school, it has grown into a broad classical university offering more than a hundred bachelor's, master's and doctoral specialties.

Plovdiv University is especially strong in the natural sciences and in mathematics and informatics: its Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics is one of the country's leading schools for computer science, software engineering, artificial intelligence and data science, while the biology, chemistry and physics faculties combine teaching with active research. Alongside these it has well-regarded programmes in economics, law, philology, history, philosophy and teacher education.

Study is mainly in Bulgarian, with selected courses in English and a one-year Bulgarian-language preparatory course for international students. Admission is by state matriculation results or university entrance exams, in several competitive rounds. Tuition is among the lowest at any Bulgarian state university — roughly €350–€500 per year for Bulgarian and EU students on state-subsidised places — and a wide range of merit, social and Erasmus+ scholarships is available. The landmark Rectorate on Tsar Asen Street, a historic building in the city centre, is the university's best-known address.

33.name: Medical University of Plovdiv
33.description: Plovdiv's public medical university (est. 1945) — one of Bulgaria's leading medical schools, teaching Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy in Bulgarian and English, with a 2,000-bed university hospital base.
33.longDescription:
The Medical University of Plovdiv (MU-Plovdiv) is a state medical university in Plovdiv, the second city of Bulgaria. It was founded in 1945 as the Medical Faculty of Plovdiv University, became an independent Medical Academy in 1950, and took its current name in 2002. Its motto is "Dedicated to Humanity", and its rector is Prof. Angel Uchikov, DMSc. Around 5,000 Bulgarian and international students study here, taught by some 690 academic staff.

The university is organised into four faculties — Medicine, Dental Medicine, Pharmacy and Public Health — together with a Medical College, a Department of Languages and Specialized Training, and a Doctoral School. It is one of the most international medical schools in Bulgaria: Medicine, Dental Medicine, Pharmacy and Nursing are all offered in English, attracting students from across Europe and beyond.

Teaching is closely tied to practice. The university's clinical base includes a university hospital with around 2,000 beds, a modern Simulation Centre, research laboratories and the Research Institute (RIMU). Its Central Library holds more than 170,000 volumes, and the university publishes the long-running peer-reviewed journal Folia Medica. A modern Auditorium Complex and a dedicated Dental Medicine building anchor the campus in central Plovdiv.

Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy are studied as long integrated master's programmes (five to six years), while the Faculty of Public Health and the Medical College train nurses, midwives, kinesitherapists, medical laboratory assistants, dental technicians and other health professionals. Tuition for the English programmes is about €10,000 per year for Medicine and Dental Medicine and €6,200 for Pharmacy, while Bulgarian and EU students on state-subsidised places pay much less — and Nursing and Midwifery are protected, tuition-free specialties. A range of scholarships, Erasmus+ mobility and dedicated support for international students is available.
